newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols held up by impending U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols held up by impending U.S. data.

text.p: A slide in implied volatility of German Bund options traded on LIFFE is being held back by the prospect of U.S. employment data later in the week, traders said on Tuesday.
Concerns are mounting that the U.S. economy may be overheating, which could lead the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates as early as the current quarter.

"No-one's keen to sell off volatility ahead of those figures, even though it does look a bit high," said a trader at a British brokerage in London. "It's keeping pretty steady and likely to remain that way until Friday."
December U.S. payrolls data were scheduled for release on Friday, and were forecast to show a rise of 192,000, compared with 118,000 in the prior month.
Volatility of February Bund options on the March Bund contract was at 6.05 percent by 1315 GMT, little changed to slightly firmer on the day.
A trader on the LIFFE floor said a Scandinavian house earlier sold 2,000 lots of the 98.00 strike February puts. More than 2,500 lots had been traded, according to LIFFE data.
The 98.50 puts were also active, with more than 1,400 lots changing hands.
March Bund futures were up six basis points at 99.68.
In the March options, a U.S. house bought 2,000 March calls at the 101.50 strike. At-the-money volatility was around 6.25 percent for March, up from around 6.00 on the previous day.
The trader on the LIFFE floor said the overall strategies observed were bullish, although an increase in put selling had started to emerge.
However, calls still outnumbered puts significantly, traders said.
Further out, April and June options on the June futures contract experienced only limited trade, and both saw volatility hold steady at 5.9/6.0 percent.
